messages.text: Martinez apologises for outburst after Wilcox talks

metadata.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology for his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.
metadata.content: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender apologises for outburst and holds talks with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender apologises for outburst and holds talks with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy after their Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox Thursday 15 October 2026 19:43, UK Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology for his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid. Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Spain, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad and said he expected more from "upstairs" after he singled out technical director Jason Wilcox. Sky Sports News understands Martinez met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, on Thursday. Head coach Michael Carrick was also present at the meeting. metadata.content: Ryan Garcia set to face US rival Teofimo Lopez next after emphatic victory over Conor Benn | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ryan Garcia set to face US rival Teofimo Lopez next after emphatic victory over Conor Benn After his spectacular stoppage of Conor Benn, Ryan Garcia is set to face Teofimo Lopez next; Benn is yet to confirm his next career move although he continues to be linked with a trilogy fight against Chris Eubank Jr; Garcia and fellow American Lopez are both welterweight world champions Thursday 15 October 2026 17:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Garcia retained his WBC world title after flooring Conor Benn heavily before forcing a stoppage victory in the second round. Fight footage courtesy of DAZN Ryan Garcia is set to face Teofimo Lopez in his next fight after his emphatic victory over Conor Benn last month. Garcia defended his WBC welterweight title with a second-round stoppage of British contender Benn in Las Vegas and is now holding talks for a fight against Lopez, Sky Sports News understands. Fellow American Lopez also holds a world title in the same division after he sealed a majority decision win over Rolando Romero to claim the WBA belt in August. messages.text: Infantino sorry for World Cup plan and set to ditch Peace Prize

metadata.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan at a three-hour FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on Thursday - and the Peace Prize he awarded to US President Donald Trump looks set to be ditched.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign Gianni Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council for his World Cup sell-off plan; FIFA president was speaking in Zurich on Thursday morning; the FA is among European leaders who still want him to resign, while UEFA has called on Infantino to release documents related to the scheme Kaveh Solhekol Chief Correspondent Thursday 15 October 2026 18:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gianni Infantino says he apologised for 'mistakes in relation to the communication and consultation process' for World Cup sell-off plan FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan at a three-hour FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on Thursday - and the Peace Prize he awarded to US President Donald Trump looks set to be ditched. Infantino's expression of regret for not telling the council about his plans earlier was not good enough for European football leaders, including FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who still want him to resign. UEFA wants Infantino to release all documents relating to the plan as they believe the 20 per cent stake in all future FIFA tournaments was being sold for a knockdown price. messages.text: Kartal through to quarter-finals in Wuhan after another stunning win

metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal thumped two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini to reach the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open.
metadata.content: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal stuns Jasmine Paolini to set up quarter-final against Elina Svitolina while Alexander Zverev continues winning form | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal stuns Jasmine Paolini to set up quarter-final against Elina Svitolina while Alexander Zverev continues winning form Sonay Kartal, in only her third tournament back from six months out with a back stress fracture upsets Jasmine Paolini in China; watch the WTA Wuhan Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Thursday 15 October 2026 15:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open clash between Sonay Kartal and Jasmine Paolini Britain's Sonay Kartal thumped two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini to reach the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open. Kartal has made a brilliant return from six months out with a back injury and dropped only two games in a 6-2 6-0 victory against 15th seed Paolini. It was an error-strewn performance from former French Open and Wimbledon runner-up Paolini and Kartal took full advantage, winning the final 11 games. messages.text: 'Not helping me or my future' - Colapinto asks fans to stop online abuse

metadata.summary: Alpine driver Franco Colapinto has asked his fanbase to stop directing online abuse at other Formula 1 drivers and figures within the sport because it is "not helping" his career.
metadata.content: Franco Colapinto: Alpine driver urges fans to stop online abuse amid concerns it is damaging his career | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Franco Colapinto: Alpine driver urges fans to stop online abuse amid concerns it is damaging his career Franco Colapinto's Alpine team have had to condemn online abuse on several occasions following contentious incidents involving the Argentine driver; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 15 October 2026 12:41, UK Image: Franco Colapinto has asked his supporters to 'change and improve' Alpine driver Franco Colapinto has asked his fanbase to stop directing online abuse at other Formula 1 drivers and figures within the sport because it is "not helping" his career. After becoming the first Argentine driver to compete in F1 for more than 20 years when he was drafted in by Williams midway through the 2024 season, Colapinto has received huge support from his home nation. However, since Colapinto joined Alpine in 2025, the team have had to issue several statements condemning online hate and abuse following incidents involving the 23-year-old driver.
